landing.heroTitle1: Know what your field is doing -
landing.heroDesc: agric-satellite-analysis is an open source crop intelligence platform: Sentinel-2 imagery, weather, soil and time fused into one explainable picture of every field you manage - with the observation, its size, its window, and the conditions behind it.
landing.cardAlert: NDVI fell 18% over 14 days, from 0.71 to 0.58.
landing.cardVerdict: Water stress, not disease. Check irrigation before you spray.
landing.multiTitle: One field, four ways to read it
landing.multiDesc: Same scene, same date, four indices. Vigour, canopy structure, soil-adjusted growth and surface water - each on a fixed scientific scale, so the same colour always means the same value across every field you own.
landing.multiCaption: The stressed patch in the north-east shows in every index - that is what tells you it is real and not a cloud artefact.
landing.seasonTitle: A whole season, scene by scene
landing.seasonDesc: Twenty-four months of Sentinel-2 backfilled on the day you draw a boundary. Green-up, peak, senescence - and the week something went wrong.
landing.layersDesc: Four observation planes stack into one geometry. Layer B reads across all of them; layer C is only ever a way out. Each boundary is a real service boundary - run the whole stack, or take the observation layer and put your own models on top.
landing.layerBoundariesDesc: Drawn, imported, or detected by the FTW model
landing.layerSatelliteDesc: Sentinel-2 at 10 m, four indices, weekly
landing.layerSoilDesc: SoilGrids 250 m worldwide, POLARIS 30 m in the US
landing.reproTitle: Every pixel traces back to a scene
landing.reproDesc: Four public steps, no black box in the middle. Every value in the UI carries the satellite, the date, the cloud cover and the colormap that produced it.
landing.repro1Desc: Element84 catalogue, filtered by geometry, date and cloud cover.
landing.repro2Desc: Index computed per scene, written to object storage as a cloud-optimised GeoTIFF.
landing.repro3Desc: Served with a fixed colormap, so two fields are always comparable.
landing.repro4Desc: Zonal statistics stored alongside the scene that produced them.
landing.reproNote: Re-run any analysis and get the same answer - or file an issue with the scene ID and someone else can reproduce it.
landing.soilDesc: Texture, pH, organic carbon, CEC and hydraulic properties for every layer down to 200 cm - pulled automatically the moment a field exists. This is what turns "NDVI is down" into "and the topsoil can't hold water".
landing.soilCaption: Clay fraction rises with depth - water sits at 30-60 cm and the topsoil dries first.
landing.hostDesc: Next.js, FastAPI, PostGIS, MinIO and TiTiler in one Docker Compose file. No Mapbox token, no per-hectare pricing, no vendor account standing between you and your own field data.
landing.host1: Runs on a free-tier Oracle Cloud VM
landing.host2: MapLibre and PMTiles - no basemap token needed
landing.host3: Multi-tenant with owner / admin / member / viewer roles
landing.host4: Simplified Chinese, English and Spanish, light and dark
landing.footerLine: Built in the open, for everyone's fields
landing.ctaDesc: From smallholders to enterprises. BSD-3-Clause, no seat limits, no lock-in, and contributions are genuinely wanted.
landing.footerTagline: Open data, open source, open to forks
landing.thanksDesc: agric-satellite-analysis is a thin layer over decades of open source and open data. These projects do the hard parts, they are free for anyone to use, and self-hosting agric-satellite-analysis means standing on their work too.
landing.thanksHostingDesc: runs openfarm.earth on an Always Free Ampere instance, the same 2 OCPU and 12 GB anyone can claim.

seo.title: agric-satellite-analysis: Open Source Crop Intelligence Platform
seo.description: Open source crop intelligence: Sentinel-2 imagery, weather and soil fused into explainable per-field insights. Self-hostable, BSD-3-Clause, no API keys.
seo.longDescription: agric-satellite-analysis is an open source crop intelligence platform. It fuses Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, daily weather and soil data into per-field insights, and shows the evidence behind every alert: which index moved, over what window, and the conditions that explain it.
seo.featureList: Sentinel-2 vegetation indices at 10 m | 24 months of history backfilled per field | Daily weather history and 7-day forecast | Soil properties by depth to 200 cm | Explained anomaly alerts | Field boundary detection from imagery | Self-hosted with Docker Compose | Multi-tenant with role-based access
seo.ogHeadline: Know what your field is doing, and why
seo.ogSubhead: Open source crop intelligence from satellite, weather and soil
seo.ogAlt: agric-satellite-analysis, open source crop intelligence from satellite, weather and soil

datasetDesc.sentinel: Multispectral optical imagery from the European Space Agency's Sentinel-2 mission: 13 bands at 10 to 60 m resolution with a five-day revisit at the equator. agric-satellite-analysis computes NDVI, EVI, SAVI and NDWI per scene from its red, near-infrared and short-wave infrared bands, and backfills 24 months of history for every field boundary.
datasetDesc.weather: Daily and hourly weather history and forecasts aggregated from national meteorological services. agric-satellite-analysis reads temperature, precipitation, evapotranspiration, wind and soil moisture from it, and derives growing degree days, reference evapotranspiration, water balance and a drought index for each field.
datasetDesc.soil: Global soil property maps predicted at 250 m resolution from a compilation of soil profile observations and environmental covariates. agric-satellite-analysis reads texture, pH, organic carbon, cation exchange capacity, bulk density and available water capacity by depth layer down to 200 cm.

faq.title: Answers before you deploy
faq.desc: The things people ask before running agric-satellite-analysis on their own fields.

what.a: agric-satellite-analysis is an open source crop intelligence platform. It fuses Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, daily weather and soil data into per-field insights, and shows the evidence behind every alert: which index moved, over what window, and the conditions that explain it.

stress.q: How does agric-satellite-analysis detect crop stress?
stress.a: It compares each new scene against the field's own history rather than a fixed threshold. When an index drops, agric-satellite-analysis reads rainfall, evapotranspiration and soil water balance for the same window, so the alert tells you whether it is water stress, not merely that something changed.

satellite.q: What satellite data does agric-satellite-analysis use?
satellite.a: Sentinel-2, the European Space Agency's 10 m multispectral mission, searched through the public Element 84 Earth Search catalogue. agric-satellite-analysis computes NDVI, EVI, SAVI and NDWI per scene, skips scenes above the cloud threshold, and backfills 24 months of history when you draw a boundary.

soil.q: What soil data does agric-satellite-analysis use?
soil.a: ISRIC SoilGrids supplies texture, pH, organic carbon, CEC and hydraulic properties worldwide at 250 m, and POLARIS supplies 30 m coverage across the United States. Both are pulled automatically for every layer down to 200 cm the moment a field boundary exists.

free.a: Yes. agric-satellite-analysis is BSD-3-Clause licensed with no seat limits, no per-hectare pricing and no vendor account. Run the whole stack yourself at no cost beyond your own server, or try the hosted demo first. No third-party API keys are required, including for the basemap.

selfhost.a: Yes, that is the default. Next.js, FastAPI, PostGIS, MinIO and TiTiler start from a single Docker Compose file on any VPS, and Terraform can provision the machine for you. The live demo runs on a free-tier 2 OCPU, 12 GB instance, which fits the entire stack.

crops.a: Cereals, pulses, oilseeds, vegetables, fibre and perennial crops each ship with a suitability profile: temperature, rainfall, pH, drainage and salinity envelopes scored against your field's real soil and climate. Profiles are plain data in the repository, so adding a crop is a pull request.

updates.q: How often is the data updated?
updates.a: Sentinel-2 revisits most fields every few days, and agric-satellite-analysis recomputes indices weekly from the newest usable scene. Weather refreshes daily alongside a 7-day forecast. Soil is fetched once per field, because soil properties change over decades rather than weeks.

indexHints.ndvi: Shows surface greenness to help assess vegetation cover and growth; declines can also reflect maturity, harvest, or cloud.
indexHints.evi: Helps distinguish dense vegetation; its scale differs from NDVI, so compare trends rather than raw values.
indexHints.ndmi: Tracks vegetation moisture, not measured soil moisture; interpret it with rainfall and field conditions.
indexHints.ndre: Tracks chlorophyll-related changes; low values can reflect yellowing, maturity, or growth stress.
indexHints.mndwi: Highlights possible surface water; ponds, irrigation, and flooded paddies can also appear as water.
indexHints.cire: Provides a relative chlorophyll signal, not a direct chlorophyll measurement or fertilizer recommendation.
indexHints.vv: Sentinel-1 co-polarized radar backscatter shows signal strength, not a crop-growth score.
indexHints.vh: Sentinel-1 cross-polarized radar backscatter; compare it with VV and observations across dates.
indexHints.drought: Uses optical indicators to flag possible water stress; verify with time trends, rainfall, and field checks. Levels use same-month baselines from currently loaded in-season scenes, so adding imagery may update earlier labels.
indexHints.flood: Date-level classification needs at least 3 comparable observations. With fewer, it will not label a date dry or as confirmed flood: water-like scenes remain a watch, and other dates are left unclassified. Single-scene VV/VH thresholds cannot confirm a flood. Each date uses only currently loaded scenes from that date and earlier; loading older history may add baseline samples, while later scenes do not rewrite earlier labels.
indexHints.savi: A vegetation index that reduces soil-background effects when plants are sparse or soil is exposed.
indexHints.ndwi: Highlights possible surface water; it does not measure soil moisture.
indexHints.sentinel2: Optical satellite imagery supports indices such as NDVI, but clouds can obscure the ground.
indexHints.sentinel1: All-weather radar observes through clouds and measures VV/VH backscatter, not photo color.

indexGuideNames.flood: Radar water candidates and time-series screening

indexGuideReadings.ndvi: Usually ranges from −1 to 1. On the same field and at a similar growth stage, higher values often mean denser green vegetation; declines can also reflect maturity, harvest, or cloud.
indexGuideReadings.evi: Higher values often indicate more vigorous vegetation under comparable conditions. EVI reduces some soil and atmospheric effects but is still affected by clouds.
indexGuideReadings.savi: Under comparable conditions, higher values usually indicate more green vegetation. It is useful during emergence or on sparsely planted fields.
indexGuideReadings.ndwi: Higher values are more likely to indicate water, though wet soil and building shadows can interfere.
indexGuideReadings.ndmi: A decline at a similar growth stage may indicate lower vegetation moisture, but can also reflect sparse vegetation or maturity.
indexGuideReadings.ndre: It can reveal leaf-color differences after the crop canopy becomes dense. A decline can reflect yellowing, maturity, or growth stress.
indexGuideReadings.cire: For the same crop and a similar stage, higher values often indicate relatively more chlorophyll. It is not a direct chlorophyll measurement; declines can be part of normal maturity.
indexGuideReadings.mndwi: Higher values are more water-like, but visible water may be a pond, irrigation, or a flooded paddy rather than a flood.
indexGuideReadings.vv: Measured in dB, VV indicates radar return strength, not crop vigor. Calm water often returns a weak signal, but wet soil and surface roughness also matter.
indexGuideReadings.vh: Also measured in dB, VH indicates signal strength. Crop structure, moisture, and the ground affect it; higher is not always better.
indexGuideReadings.drought: The map separates mild, moderate, and severe signals. The chart below shows NDVI over time. An unassessed date or missing data does not mean there is no drought.
indexGuideReadings.flood: Pixel colors show single-scene water-like signal strength. Date-level classification needs at least 3 comparable observations; with fewer, only water-like scenes remain a watch and other dates are unclassified, not dry. The chart shows VV backscatter, not water depth; irrigation, flooded paddies, ponds, and wet soil can look similar.
indexGuideReadings.sentinel2: Useful for vegetation growth, moisture, and surface color. Clouds can block the view, so clear imagery is not available every day.
indexGuideReadings.sentinel1: Provides VV and VH radar backscatter used in water screening. Radar colors represent signal strength, not the colors of an ordinary photograph.

indexGuideActions.ndvi: Compare several dates for the same field, then inspect low-value areas. NDVI is not a yield score, and a low value alone does not prove damage.
indexGuideActions.evi: Compare its trend with NDVI during vigorous growth. Their scales differ, so do not compare raw values directly.
indexGuideActions.savi: Compare dates on the same field. Low values are common when seedlings are small, so consider the planting date.
indexGuideActions.ndwi: Check the original image and nearby dates. Rule out existing ponds before investigating new water.
indexGuideActions.ndmi: If it declines over several dates, compare rainfall, NDVI, and field soil conditions before checking for water stress.
indexGuideActions.ndre: Inspect persistently low areas in the field. Do not use this index alone to diagnose a nutrient deficiency.
indexGuideActions.cire: Compare it with NDRE and field observations to prioritize scouting; do not convert it directly into a fertilizer rate.
indexGuideActions.mndwi: On clear dates, compare the mapped water edge. In cloudy periods, use radar water candidates and compare before and after rainfall.
indexGuideActions.vv: Focus on change across dates for the same field, and compare with VH or water-candidate results. Do not infer crop vigor from signal level alone.
indexGuideActions.vh: Use it as a supplement during cloudy periods and compare it with VV and other dates; it does not predict yield by itself.
indexGuideActions.drought: Check whether the signal persists across dates, then compare recent rainfall and field soil before planning irrigation.
indexGuideActions.flood: Check the observation date and relative orbit, compare the same location before and after rainfall, and verify terrain, drainage, and field conditions.
indexGuideActions.sentinel2: Prefer dates with little cloud. When clouds are heavy, try another date or consult Sentinel-1 radar observations.
indexGuideActions.sentinel1: Use it to screen for surface change and possible water when persistent cloud makes optical imagery unclear.

scene.label: Scene / observation
scene.description: A satellite record of the ground. The date is when it was observed, not necessarily today.

cloud.label: Cloud cover / clear observation
cloud.description: Cloud cover is the obscured share; lower values usually mean a clearer view. Clear observations have less cloud obstruction.

decloud.label: Cloud removal
decloud.description: Other observations are used to estimate what clouds obscure. It is a supplement, not a clear photo captured on that date.

heatmap.label: Heatmap / pixel
heatmap.description: Map colors represent an index or candidate class. A pixel is a small image cell; read the legend for each index.

mean.label: Mean / time series
mean.description: The mean averages valid observations across the field and may hide local variation. A time series connects values across dates.

season.label: Growing season / window
season.description: The period from planting through the end of this crop cycle. Compare growth with its emergence, vigorous-growth, and maturity stages in mind.

landReportTab.chartWeights: Weights: crop 25%, soil 20%, vigor 20%, weather 15%, flood safety 10%, drought safety 10%.
landReportTab.noScorecardHint: Generate a land report first. The chart uses that report's real scores, not sample numbers.
landReportTab.legacyNoScorecard: This report was saved without dimension scores
landReportTab.legacyNoScorecardHint: Generate a new land report to fill the hexagon.
landReportTab.cdfinancePanelHint: Generation automatically uses the current login, field group, and base information to fetch the site questionnaire and NPK.
landReportTab.cdfinanceGroupPlaceholder: e.g. 3232; leave blank to resolve from agri tags
landReportTab.cdfinanceToken: Bearer Token (temporary; not stored in server config)
landReportTab.siteAdmissionMissingHint: No cached site-admission questionnaire; generation will try the current login automatically.
landReportTab.cdfinanceHrBaseIdPlaceholder: e.g. 10; leave blank for server CDFINANCE_HR_BASE_ID
landReportTab.aiReferenceDisclaimer: AI reference only · not an admission decision
landReportTab.aiReferenceHint: For discussion only. Does not replace the program overall score and must not be used as a site-admission conclusion.
landReportTab.generationSettingsDialogHint: Choose the crop and history range, then confirm to pull data and generate the PDF.

overviewPage.title: China overview
overviewPage.subtitle: Drought / flood / weak growth · country→province→city→county
overviewPage.clickMapHint: Click the map to drill down
overviewPage.dailySchedule: Check new S1/S2 scenes daily at 23:00 China time; refresh after ingestion
overviewPage.showingPrevious: Today's snapshot is pending; showing the latest saved result
overviewPage.partialSnapshot: Incomplete data; check failed jobs and observation gaps
overviewPage.noSnapshots: No saved snapshot for this date. Missing data does not mean no hazard. Existing scenes are available in Date range.
overviewPage.historyHint: Affected parcels; blank dates have no snapshot. Unknown shows drought/flood gaps; * marks incomplete data. Select a date to view its saved result.
overviewPage.coverageCounts: Observed that day: {today} · Carried forward: {carried} · Unknown: {unknown}
overviewPage.coverageHint: Latest usable scene within 60 days of the reporting date. Expired, cloudy, or out-of-season drought observations are unknown. New satellite observations are not available every day.
overviewPage.cropHint: Sets weak-growth phenology months only; does not filter parcels by planted crop
overviewPage.weakParcelsEmpty: No weak-growth parcels for this region/filters

seasonGrowthReport.title: Season growth report
seasonGrowthReport.description: Summarize S2/S1 remote-sensing facts for a custom season window, with optional materials. Numbers are computed in code; the LLM only writes interpretation (PDF still works without an API key).
seasonGrowthReport.materialSizeLimit: Each file can be up to 20 MiB. Larger files are skipped.
seasonGrowthReport.materialTooLarge: Each material file must be 20 MiB or smaller.
seasonGrowthReport.datesRequired: Please set start and end dates
seasonGrowthReport.endBeforeStart: The end date must be on or after the start date.
seasonGrowthReport.dateRangeTooLong: The report window cannot exceed 10 years (3,660 days).
seasonGrowthReport.futureDateNotAllowed: The report end date cannot be later than today.
seasonGrowthReport.dateRangeLimit: Report windows can cover up to 10 years (3,660 days, including both dates) and cannot end in the future.
seasonGrowthReport.empty: No season growth report yet — pick a window and generate.
seasonGrowthReport.noteFacts: Facts (scene counts, NDVI/NDMI, drought/flood, harvest) are computed from products — never invented by the LLM.
seasonGrowthReport.noteLlm: AI narrative needs BAILIAN_API_KEY; without it the PDF still includes facts and charts.
seasonGrowthReport.cdfinanceReuseHint: The current login, field group, and base information are passed automatically before generation; nothing needs to be entered manually.

reportPreview.title: Full assessment report
reportPreview.failed: Unable to load the report. Retry or download the PDF.
reportPreview.pageFailed: Unable to render this page. Please download the PDF.

landReportsHome.title: Land assessment reports
landReportsHome.selectHint: Select a land parcel to view or generate an assessment report.

remoteSensingOnboarding.unavailable: This step is not available on the current page yet. Retry or skip it.

nav.title: Start from Project remote sensing
nav.body: Use the top navigation to open your planting projects.

project.title: Open a project
project.body: Choose a planting project with fields so you can continue to the field list.

land.title: Choose a field
land.body: Select a field to open its details. Check the boundary and crop first.

ndvi.title: Open the Remote sensing tab
ndvi.body: Switch to Remote sensing to pick dates and view growth layers.

date.title: Pick an observation date
date.body: Click a date or a point on the chart. Prefer dates with low cloud cover.

growth.title: Start with NDVI, then compare
growth.body: Use NDVI, drought, and flood at the bottom of the map. A low value can also mean emergence, maturity, or clouds.

report.title: Review the land report
report.body: If a change persists, open the land report and verify it in the field.

projectMonitoring.missingArea: Area missing for {count}; known area only
projectMonitoring.areaBasis: Sum of parcel areas in scope
projectMonitoring.riskAreaNote: Parcel area involved, not damaged area
projectMonitoring.riskAreaShare: {value}% of area in scope; not damaged area
projectMonitoring.unmarkedNote: No boundary is available to locate this parcel.
projectMonitoring.noCurrentAlerts: The current observation shows no actionable anomaly.
projectMonitoring.cannotAssess: There is not enough valid imagery to assess current risk.
projectMonitoring.verificationNote: Alerts need verification; closing a record does not confirm recovery.
projectMonitoring.freshnessRule: Status is based on quality-checked S2 optical observations from the last {days} days.
projectMonitoring.dataGap: There is not enough valid imagery to evaluate the freshness window.
projectMonitoring.comparison: Changes are compared with the valid observation on {date}.
projectMonitoring.noComparison: No previous valid observation for comparison.
projectMonitoring.moreAlerts: See full parcel details for more alerts.
projectMonitoring.loadFailed: The complete parcel list could not be loaded. Please retry.
projectMonitoring.missingProject: Project ID is missing. Open a project from the list.
projectMonitoring.monitoringUnavailable: Monitoring is unavailable; risk and alert totals are unknown. Parcel information remains available. Refresh to retry.
projectMonitoring.scopeNote: Statistics, list and map share the same filters
projectMonitoring.search: Search name, ID, crop or owner
projectMonitoring.noBoundaries: These parcels have no boundaries. View them in the list.

adminOps.title: Download machines and scheduled tasks
adminOps.description: Use claim heartbeats to verify download machines, then trigger and track key scheduled tasks.
adminOps.triggered: Task queued. Its status will update automatically.
adminOps.loadFailed: Failed to load operations data. Please try again.
adminOps.workersDescription: Every successful claim, including an empty claim, updates the heartbeat. More than three missed polling cycles and at least 30 seconds mark it stale; twice that age marks it possibly offline.
adminOps.noWorkers: No download machine has reported a claim heartbeat yet.
adminOps.tasksDescription: Scheduled jobs and API-side data sync tasks can be triggered here and tracked to completion.
adminOps.smartBackfillHint: Use a parcel list (one per line or comma-separated) or an inclusive ID range. Missing land_parcels rows are filled from Smart before S1/S2 history is queued. At most 1,000 queried parcels are processed, and the run details list the parcels actually queued.
adminOps.smartSelectionRequired: Enter either a land ID list, or both range endpoints. Do not mix the two modes.
adminOps.smartYearsInvalid: Years must be an integer from 1 to 10.
adminOps.satelliteHistoryHint: Leave blank for all active parcels. Each run dynamically groups the selected parcels into 10×10 km windows, fetches S1/S2 COG data, and stores only parcel-level results.
adminOps.satelliteHistoryLandListPlaceholder: Optional land_id list; leave blank for all active parcels
adminOps.satelliteHistoryYearsInvalid: History backfill years must be an integer from 1 to 10.
adminOps.runsDescription: This includes automatic scheduled runs and manually triggered runs; status refreshes every 10 seconds, and task names expand to full details.
adminOps.jobsSummaryDetail: Counts include every status; pagination exposes the full history
adminOps.workItemsSummaryDetail: Includes pending, leased, completed, and failed items; pagination exposes the full history
adminOps.executionLoadFailed: Failed to load job and work-item execution data.
adminOps.jobsDescription: Shows task status, land, progress, and errors; expand a task type for full details.
adminOps.workItemsDescription: Shows worker claims, leases, retries, progress, and results; expand an item type for full details.
adminOps.detailLoadFailed: Failed to load details. Please try again.
adminOps.parentJobsSummaryDetail: Grouped by parent task; failed children do not hide the parent result
adminOps.executionGroupsDescription: Only parent tasks are listed here. Open a task to inspect every child job and work item.
adminOps.noChildren: This parent task has no linked child tasks.
adminOps.downloadWorkerWorkItemsHint: All Work Items dispatched to download workers are collected here; expand an item to inspect its owner, lease, retries, error, and full payload.

parcelInsights.title: Field insights
parcelInsights.description: Compare fields, review observed growing windows, and revisit seasons and farming actions. Historical results can be saved as reports; recent analysis stays on the page.
parcelInsights.selectionHint: Select 1–20 fields. For detailed comparison, choose 2–4 fields growing similar crops.
parcelInsights.historicalHint: Reports use historical observations before the cutoff. Today’s observations and current alerts are excluded.
parcelInsights.recentHint: Recent results are shown on the page only. Actual valid satellite observation dates determine freshness.
parcelInsights.seasonSettings: Observed growing windows and manual review
parcelInsights.seasonHint: Valid imagery identifies candidate growth cycles. A manual window takes priority. Canopy changes do not establish exact sowing, maturity, or harvest dates.
parcelInsights.multipleSeasons: Multiple complete cycles found. Review the analysis and manually select the cycle to compare.
parcelInsights.serviceHint: Record actions that actually occurred. Records are retained with the historical analysis. Changes do not establish causation or yield gains.
parcelInsights.snapshotHint: After changing inputs, run analysis again. Existing results retain their original inputs.
parcelInsights.firstFour: The chart shows the first 4 fields; cards and statistics include all selected fields.
parcelInsights.matchedCount: Matched {count} groups of nearby observation dates.
parcelInsights.differentCrops: Crops differ or are unknown. View differences without ranking performance.
parcelInsights.rainCoverage: Rainfall recorded on {count}/{total} days. Missing data are not zero.
parcelInsights.chooseReference: Enter a reference year and analyze again.
parcelInsights.progressHint: Counts cover selected fields only. These are observed signals at the period end, not confirmed planting or harvest completion rates. Fields lacking evidence remain unknown.
parcelInsights.noEvents: Add farming action records above and analyze again to review before-and-after changes.
parcelInsights.empty: Select fields and a historical period to create a reviewable, saved analysis.
parcelInsights.inferenceSummary: Detected {count} cycles, including {complete} complete cycles; {observations} valid observation dates.
parcelInsights.windowFilled: The selected window has been filled in. Review or edit the dates above.
parcelInsights.partialWindowFilled: Known dates have been filled in. Missing boundaries are blank; complete them above.
parcelInsights.observedWindowFilled: The first and last observation dates filled this window. They are not exact sowing or harvest dates; review them manually.
parcelInsights.chooseWindow: Choose a cycle to fill in. Partial cycles fill only the known dates.
parcelInsights.noCompleteWindow: No candidate cycle is available. Enter dates manually or adjust the analysis period and retry.
parcelInsights.completeDatesHint: Complete the manual window start and end dates, or disable the manual window before analyzing.
parcelInsights.inferenceMismatch: The result does not match the current parcel or date range. Please detect again.
